docs.title: MCP Cross Exam
docs.text: Audit one MCP server and write a scored report. The repository is smusali/mcp-cross-exam.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
pipx install mcp-cross-exam
uvx mcp-cross-exam --help

docs.title: Try it
docs.text:
Start the local server, then audit it. The server defaults to session.expired-empty-success and schema.undeclared-required-arg:

mcp-cross-exam fixture serve --http 127.0.0.1:8765
mcp-cross-exam http://127.0.0.1:8765/mcp

--clean serves no defects, and that audit exits 0. A server with findings exits 3 unless --fail-on says otherwise. Exit codes are in Usage.

docs.title: Probes
docs.text:
Family What a finding means Transport and session Negotiation, headers, reconnects, stream resume, or an expired session is wrong. Schema A tool definition, argument, error, or description does not match what the server does.

The catalog is in Methodology.

docs.title: Safety
docs.text:
Stdio and a loopback host are local. Any other host must match [target] allow, and --target-is-not-production still needs that match. Credentials come from the environment and are redacted from the run directory.

Not a pentest, not a load tester, not a proxy or gateway, and not a hosted service. Limits of the auditor are in Limitations.

Where to go next:

  • Usage for every command, every config key, and exit codes.
  • Methodology for the probe catalog, scoring, and false positives.
  • Changelog for what shipped.

docs.title: Changelog
docs.text:
All notable changes to this project are documented in this file.

The format is based on Keep a Changelog, and this project adheres to Semantic Versioning.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• mcp-cross-exam <endpoint> audits one MCP server over stdio, streamable HTTP, or legacy HTTP+SSE.
  • Transport and session probes check negotiation, capabilities, reconnects, stream resume, and expired sessions.
  • Schema probes compare tool definitions, arguments, errors, and descriptions with what the server does.
  • A production guard refuses any host that is not loopback and not in [target] allow.
  • Each run writes a scored report.json, a static report.html, and redacted evidence.
  • --fail-on and documented exit codes let a CI job fail on findings.
  • probes, config, snapshot, and replay subcommands plan, configure, pin, and repeat an audit.
  • fixture serve defaults to the two demo findings, and --clean serves none.
  • PyPI releases carry provenance attestations.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
uv sync --frozen --group dev
uv run pytest
uv run ruff check .
uv run ruff format --check .
uv run mypy --strict src/mcp_cross_exam tests tools
uv run lint-imports

The documentation site uses the docs group:

uv sync --frozen --group docs && uv run mkdocs build

Tests may open sockets only to 127.0.0.1 and ::1.

CI runs checkOwners. @smusali is the sole owner, so a single expert does not fail the job.

docs.title: Layers
docs.text:
flowchart TD
  cli[cli] --> runner[runner]
  cli --> report[report]
  cli --> fixture[fixture]
  runner --> probes[probes]
  runner --> findings[findings]
  report --> findings
  probes --> audit[schema audit]
  probes --> transport[transport]
  probes --> types[types]
  findings --> types
  transport --> types
  fixture --> types

Higher boxes may import lower ones. report does not import runner. fixture does not import the schema auditor. Only cli opens a stdio or HTTP adapter.

docs.title: Adding a probe
docs.text: Add the probe class next to the others and register it. Set impact, summary, and spec. Add one fixture defect with the same id, and keep fixture serve --clean free of findings. A probe that cannot be triggered, or that fires on a clean server, is not done.

docs.title: Release
docs.text:
1. Move Unreleased to a version section of one sentence per entry.
  2. Set __version__ to that version.
  3. Tag vX.Y.Z. A tag that contains rc publishes to TestPyPI. Any other tag publishes to PyPI.
  4. The release workflow builds the wheel, checks the changelog, and uploads attestations.
  5. The docs workflow deploys that version and points latest at it.

docs.title: Methodology
docs.text: A run connects, lists tools, selects probes, and records each call. A probe returns a draft when the server disagrees with its contract. The report turns that draft into a finding with a severity, a blast radius, and a penalty. The score starts at 100 and subtracts penalties.

docs.title: Catalog
docs.text:
Probe Severity Impact transport.version-negotiation high the client and server disagree on the protocol revision transport.capabilities-honesty high the client calls a feature the server did not declare transport.required-headers high a tool call proceeds without the routing headers transport.unknown-method high an unknown method is treated as success session.token-expired-empty-success high agent silently degrades session.expired-not-404 high agent silently degrades session.expired-empty-success high agent silently degrades transport.resume-gap medium the client misses events after a dropped stream transport.reconnect-fails high a retry does not see the same tool result schema.lint.invalid-schema high the model cannot form a valid call schema.lint.root-not-object medium the model cannot form a valid call schema.lint.required-not-declared high the model omits a required argument and loops schema.lint.missing-description low the model guesses what the tool does schema.lint.name-invalid low the model cannot address the tool by name schema.lint.duplicate-name high the model cannot tell the tools apart schema.lint.annotation-contradiction medium the model treats a write as a read schema.lint.unbounded-string info the model can send an unbounded string schema.lint.hidden-instructions info hidden text can steer the model schema.error-shape.unknown-tool low an unknown tool name is not rejected schema.tool-list-unstable high the model caches a tool list that changes schema.tool-set-unstable high a tool disappears between connections schema.tool-order-unstable low tool order changes and the model picks the wrong one schema.pagination-broken medium the model stops after the first page schema.list-cache-hints-invalid low the client caches a list it should refetch schema.list-changed-not-notified medium the model keeps a stale tool list schema.definition-drift medium the tool contract changed since the snapshot schema.undeclared-required-arg high the model omits a required argument and loops schema.required-not-enforced medium the model can skip a required argument schema.extra-args-silently-accepted medium an extra argument is dropped without an error schema.silent-coercion high the model receives a value it did not send schema.constraint-not-enforced medium a value outside the schema is accepted schema.error-shape.validation-as-protocol-error medium the model treats a bad argument as a broken protocol schema.error-shape.unactionable medium the model cannot tell which argument to fix schema.error-shape.internal-leak medium an error string exposes server internals schema.output-nonconformant high the model reads a result the schema does not describe schema.description-param-mismatch medium the model sends an argument the schema does not define schema.description-contract-broken medium the result breaks a limit the description stated schema.example-fails medium the model copies an example the server rejects schema.annotation-readonly-violated high a read tool changes server state

transport.stdout-pollution and transport.deprecated-sse are transport findings, not probes.

docs.title: Severity and score
docs.text:
Severity weights are info 0, low 1, medium 4, high 10, and critical 25. Effect multipliers are read 1, write 2, destructive 3, and external 4. Scope multipliers are user 1, tenant 2, and global 3. The raw penalty is the product of those three.

Findings that share a tool and a family are ordered by raw penalty. The first keeps its penalty, and each later finding keeps half of its raw penalty, rounded down. A tool's penalties are then capped at min(100, max(25, 300 / tool count)). The score is 100 minus the sum of the penalties.

A high finding on a write tool scoped to one user is 10 * 2 * 1 = 20. One such finding scores 80.

docs.title: False positives
docs.text: Hidden-instruction lint matches steering text in a description, so a warning that names the pattern can look like the defect. A description contract is only a finding when the result breaks a limit the description stated. Extra arguments are a finding only when additionalProperties is not true and the server accepts the extra key. Silent coercion is a finding when the server returns a value the client did not send. The read-only observer calls a read tool twice and reports a finding only when the second result shows a write.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text: mcp-cross-exam <endpoint> audits one server. --help prints the options for the current command.

docs.title: run
docs.text: Option Meaning endpoint Streamable HTTP URL. A bare URL is the same as run. --sse Legacy HTTP+SSE endpoint. -- Stdio command after this separator. --cwd Working directory for a stdio command. --env Set KEY=VALUE for a stdio command. --env-from Copy an environment variable into a stdio command. --bearer-env Environment variable holding a bearer token. --expired-bearer-env Environment variable holding an expired bearer token. --header-env Send a header from an environment variable (Header=ENV). --ca-bundle CA bundle for TLS. --protocol-version Offer only this protocol revision. --probe Run probes whose ids match this glob. Repeat to combine. --family Run probes in this family. --skip Skip this probe id. --seed Seed the run. --tool Limit the audit to one tool. --jobs How many tools to examine at once. Default 4. --config Config file. --read-only Skip write and destructive calls. --allow-writes Allow writes when the guard is overridden. --target-is-not-production Audit an allow-listed host that is not production. --fail-on-incomplete Exit 3 when the run is partial. --fail-on Fail when a finding is at or above this severity. Default high. --out-dir Directory for the report, evidence, and transcripts. --snapshot Compare tool definitions with this snapshot. --version Print version facts. --json Print machine-readable output. --quiet Suppress non-error output. --no-color Disable color. --exit-zero Exit 0 when the result is findings.

docs.title: probes
docs.text: Command Meaning probes list Print the registered probes. --json prints JSON. probes plan Show which probes would run. Does not call tools.

docs.title: config
docs.text: Command Meaning config show Print the effective config. --config selects a file. --json prints JSON. config init Write a commented config from tools/list.

docs.title: snapshot
docs.text: Command Meaning snapshot write List tools and write a snapshot. --out sets the path.

docs.title: replay
docs.text: Argument Meaning transcript JSON-RPC JSONL transcript. endpoint Streamable HTTP endpoint.

docs.title: fixture
docs.text: Option Meaning fixture serve --stdio Speak MCP on standard input. --http Listen on HOST:PORT for streamable HTTP. --sse Listen on HOST:PORT for legacy HTTP+SSE. --era Protocol revision to speak. --defects Comma-separated probe ids, all, or none. The default is session.expired-empty-success,schema.undeclared-required-arg. --clean Serve no defects. --token-ttl-s Seconds before the valid bearer expires. fixture mint-token --expired Print the expired token.

docs.title: Config keys
docs.text: Key Meaning target.url Endpoint used when the command line omits one. target.allow Hosts the guard accepts besides loopback. auth.bearer_env Environment variable for the bearer token. auth.expired_bearer_env Environment variable for an expired bearer token. auth.header_env Map of header name to environment variable. probes.select Probe id globs to run. probes.skip Probe ids to skip. probes.severity Override a probe severity. probes.target_tool Tool the transport and session probes call. budget.wall_clock_s Stop the run after this many seconds. budget.max_calls_per_tool Cap calls to one tool. budget.call_timeout_s Timeout for one call. tools.<name>.effect read, write, destructive, or external. tools.<name>.scope user, tenant, or global.

docs.title: Run directory
docs.text: The default directory is .mcp-cross-exam/runs/<run-id>/. Set MCP_CROSS_EXAM_RUNS to move it. Each run writes report.json, report.html, evidence.jsonl, and transcripts/.

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text: Code Meaning 0 No findings at or above the fail-on severity 1 Internal error 2 Usage or config error, including the production guard 3 Findings at or above the fail-on severity 4 Target unreachable, or the connection or handshake failed before any probe ran 130 Interrupted

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
The auditor is black box. It sees JSON-RPC on the wire. For a stdio server it also reads stderr. It does not read server source, files, or process memory.

Hints are hints. readOnlyHint, destructiveHint, and openWorldHint are labels from the server, not proof. The report marks each blast radius value as configured, declared, observed, or default so a hint is not shown as a fact. A behavior check, such as a read tool that changes state, is a separate finding from the hint itself.

Description checks are deterministic. They compare text patterns with the schema and with tool results. They do not decide whether the prose is true beyond those patterns. A description can mention a date format or a limit while documenting something else, and those cases are called out as false positive modes in the methodology.

This is not a pentest. It does not guess credentials, bypass authentication, or try to exploit the host. This is not a load tester. It does not flood the server or measure capacity. The budget exists to stop the audit, not to stress the target.

These probe families are not covered: idempotency, latency, data handling, auth and scope, and concurrency. The score is one server's own run. It is not a comparison across servers.
